entries.title: Research as Mandatory Pre-Planning Step — Governance Design
entries.description: Content to resolve: (1) What do we already have about making research a mandatory step before planning? (2) Where is research optimally positioned in the CDS build sequence and for which categories of decisions? (3) What governance mechanism makes research a DEFAULT step, not an optional one — so that 'planning something' automatically triggers a research gate rather than depending on Builder discipline. The goal is to make research a HUMBLE STEP embedded in the process, not a choice made each time. Without this, planning happens with incomplete information by default. Design session needed. Candidate placement: before any new scope opens, before any corespine design, before any new rule ratification. Candidate form: POST /api/research/declare (must file a research record before planning gate opens).

entries.title: Chicken-and-Egg Design Method — Three-Draft Pattern for Circular Dependencies
entries.description: When facing circular design dependencies (schema needs wizard, wizard needs schema, gate needs contract, contract needs gate), the method is: (1) create three draft documents — schema, wizard, and a third governing doc — intentionally lightweight, explicitly deletable. (2) Spread the logic out of your head and into documents — even rough documents. (3) Once spread out, review all three with expert personas (Yariv top-expert review). Interesting cross-document insights emerge that are invisible when the logic stays internal. (4) Modify or delete freely — the drafts are not commitments. Governor note: 'allow ourselves not to be so heavy.' This method applies to any CDS design session where the root of the next feature can't be determined without a prototype of the feature itself.
entries.session_target: CTX:DESIGN_METHOD — apply when circular dependency detected

entries.title: Haiku Run Protocol v2 — Add 3 Missing Expert Agents + Context-Assembler step
entries.description: The current Haiku Run (5 agents) is missing 3 expert lenses and a grounding step. Required additions: (1) CONTEXT-ASSEMBLER (Step 0): Sonnet orchestrator reads all relevant CDS files before any agent runs and produces a 'what_exists' package that all agents receive. This prevents agents from running blind. (2) HAIKU-OSSOT-STABILITY: Expert in One Source of Truth, consolidation, and stability. Reads OSSOT doc + append-only records + existing constitutional docs. Checks: does this proposal create duplicate sources? Does it maintain OSSOT where it already exists? Does it violate append-only? (3) HAIKU-CDS-COMPATIBILITY (MOST CRITICAL): Reads actual codebase files (types.ts, rules.ts, engine.ts, constitutionals) and checks the proposal against what actually exists in code. Not a conceptual review — a code-level compatibility check. Outputs: what types need to be added? what rules would conflict? what gate changes are required? (4) HAIKU-SYNERGY: Runs AFTER all other Haiku agents complete. Reads all agent outputs. Finds cross-cutting connections, missed synergies, and enhancements that no single lens spotted. This is the pre-Opus consolidation step. Full protocol: STEP-0 (Context-Assembler) → STEP-1 (all Haiku in parallel, each receiving what_exists package) → STEP-1b (HAIKU-SYNERGY reads all STEP-1 outputs) → STEP-2 (Opus holistic) → STEP-3 (Builder MD).

entries.title: Core Council Corespine — Design Session Required
entries.description: Concept: A permanent, structured governance council that integrates AI expert agents + external advisors + the Governor into a single decision-making body for architectural reviews. Components to design: (1) CS-COUNCIL family (or function under CS-GOVERNANCE): governing the council's operating rules. (2) Member Registry: AI expert agents by domain (STABILITY, SCALABILITY, GOVERNANCE, EFFICIENCY, STRUCTURAL, OSSOT, CDS-COMPATIBILITY, SYNERGY) + external advisors by name/domain. (3) Orchestrator Policy: predefined rules for when to convene (decision types, trigger thresholds), how to weight different inputs, aggregation rules for conflicting signals. (4) Dashboard: all council runs, findings, dispositions, GOV decisions made from council input — one source of truth for all expert guidance received. (5) Audit trail: which advisor reviewed what, their recommendation, the Governor's response, and the ratification outcome. The council is NOT a chatbot or ad-hoc AI run — it is a constitutional governance mechanism with predictable, policy-governed behavior. Design questions: Does it live under CS-GOVERNANCE or as its own corespine? Who can trigger a council run (Governor only? Builder can request?)? How does external advisor input enter the platform (QUARANTINE first for translation, then classification)? Candidate session: Phase 1 design, before external advisor onboarding begins.

entries.title: CS-TEMPLATE Semantic Guards — Phase 2 artifact (CSP input absorbed)
entries.description: From CSP OPUS review: R2 (satisfiability check) gives syntactic soundness but cannot catch semantic drift under syntactic soundness. Example: Layer 2 changes audit_trail schema in a way that passes R2 (still REQUIRED, still valid) but removes ratification_id — breaking every GOVERNANCE instance's downstream intent. Solution: semantic guards — invariants that downstream instances register as dependencies ('I depend on the semantic meaning of audit_trail.ratification_id being present'). Any ancestor change that violates a registered guard produces a HELD finding. This is a Phase 2 artifact. Do NOT block Phase 1 on it. Phase 1: R2 gives syntactic soundness. Phase 2: semantic guard registry gives semantic soundness. Design session needed: schema for the guard registry, how guards register, how they integrate with the ratification gate, lifecycle of a guard when the instance it protects is deprecated.

entries.title: CS-TEMPLATE Lazy Instance Materialization — Design Session (CSPS suggestion vs CDS DNA conflict)
entries.description: CSPS Opus-25 suggested: treat Layer 4 instances as lazy projections materialized on-demand rather than registered, declared objects. Benefits: reduces cascade surface, gives Governor more intervention time, defers resolution to latest possible moment. CONFLICT WITH CDS DNA: CDS requires every element to receive a CR-ID at classification time (append-only record model). Lazy instances have no CR-ID until materialization — this is a governance identity conflict. The question is not whether lazy materialization is useful (it is) but how it reconciles with: (1) the classification gate requirement that every element is classified before it exists, (2) the append-only CR-ID model that creates a record at classification, (3) RULE-CLASS which requires all inputs to be classified before they reach the platform. Design session needed to decide: (a) are template instances classified at declaration time or at materialization time? (b) if at declaration, is the lazy projection just an optimization for storage (the CR-ID exists, the RTM is generated lazily)? (c) if at materialization, how does RULE-CLASS apply? This is a Phase 1 design question — must be answered before instance registration endpoint is built.
